incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: 14 Her c period on the confirmed tab
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: The confirmed tab has 14 Her c at P=9886 d, a=9.037 AU. NASA's default solution is 15732 d (Feng et al. 2022); Benedict et al. 2023 give 52160+/-1028 d; OEC still flags c 'Controversial' although JWST has imaged it (Bardalez Gagliuffi et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.09201). The writer may want to refresh the confirmed row.

NASA pscomppars has pl_controv_flag=1 for HD 140901 b (queried 2026-09-27). Harada et al. 2024 (SPORES-HWO II, Appendix C.6 and Table 8) list it as a 'Disputed planet candidate' that their RVs do not recover. It sits on the confirmed tab. By the brief's rule (a published planet that is disputed) it could be moved to Unconfirmed as ambiguous; the writer's call.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: HD 115404 A b and c are called disputed
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: Harada et al. 2024 (Appendix C.5) cannot recover either Feng 2022 planet from 95 ELODIE/HIRES/SOPHIE RVs and treat both as disputed because the discovery paper gives no system-specific analysis. NASA does not flag them. For the writer's judgement.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: HD 99492 c row on the confirmed tab is a hybrid
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: The confirmed tab lists HD 99492 c with P=4970 d and a=5.4 AU (the refuted Meschiari 2011 signal) but Msini=17.9 Me (the Stalport 2023 value for the real c). The real c is P=95.233 d (NASA pscomppars, exoplanet.eu; Stalport et al. 2023, arXiv:2308.05669). The row should be P~95.2 d, a~0.4 AU (writer to derive).

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.item: HD 114386 c row on the confirmed tab is a hybrid
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: The confirmed tab lists HD 114386 c with P=1046 d (the old OEC value, 1.19 MJ) but mass 118 Me (0.37 MJ, Wu et al. 2026). Wu et al. 2026 (AJ 171, 189; arXiv:2601.11280, Sect. 4.3) put c at 444.8 d, a=1.05 AU, e=0.10, Msini 0.37 MJ; NASA pscomppars agrees (444.0 d).

The 24.56 d Laliotis 2023 candidate is recovered by Harada et al. 2024 (24.567 d, K=0.632 m/s, Msini 2.3 Me), from largely the same data plus 10 HIRES nights; they also prefer a quadratic trend. Included in the candidate record as supporting evidence.
